name: spellkave_move
label: Spellkave Move
description: Move the active actor — exactly one addressing mode per call. Preferred: {rev, handle}, a stable-identity scene exit handle copied VERBATIM (both fields) from that exit's own row in spellkave_scene — the SAME exit keeps the SAME handle across re-reads and ticks; `rev` gates freshness of that ONE exit only, never the whole scene. Compatibility: {edge_id}, an adjacent-exit identifier when you do not have a scene handle. Movement is ATTEMPT-based: every exit is tried, and the world gives the authoritative verdict. The scene listing's `traversal_gates` and this tool's own `traversal_gates` echo (rev+handle mode only) are map info about what LOOKED likely, never permission. In rev+handle mode, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (prose of what the actor perceived — an authored node description, or the region's own description only when the move crossed into a different region, never repeated within the same one — or null + observation_gap when no authorized source backs this outcome); a rejection carries `receipt.move.reason` and `receipt.move.failure_detail`, never a throw. In edge_id mode, the result is a flatter `{status, actor_id, edge_id, from_node, to_node, observed_at_tick}` shape, with `reason`/`failure_detail` on rejection. Movement is never turn-gated: a move may be accepted even while `my_turn` is false. In rev+handle mode, on an ADMITTED dispatch (an immediate arrival OR a promoted long-running 'travelling' walk) with a host world-event builder wired, the result also carries `consequences`: same-tick, same-transaction WorldEvents THIS move deterministically caused (e.g. a travel-cost resource spend) — a THIRD register, distinct from `receipt`/`observation` (the reducer's own outcome) and from a LATER `pushes` drain off the same builder (world news, including this move's own delayed arrival). Omitted entirely when no builder is wired; `[]` when wired but nothing was caused. A move longer than your reach returns outcome "travelling" and takes several ticks: pass wait_for_arrival_ms to wait for the arrival in the same call, or spellkave_scene with wait_for_arrival_ms to keep waiting; do not poll.

as_body_id.description: Observed non-presence body to act as using frontier.impersonate; the server checks scope and consent.

rev.description: Scene-handle mode: the exit's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_scene — not the listing envelope's top-level rev. Required together with handle; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode.

handle.description: Scene-handle mode: stable scene exit handle, e.g. s:exit:32, from spellkave_scene. Required together with rev; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode.

edge_id.description: Adjacent-exit mode: identifier of an adjacent exit from where you are. Prefer rev+handle instead — this mode exists when you do not have a scene handle.

wait_for_arrival_ms.description: Optional, scene-handle mode. A move longer than your reach becomes a journey of several ticks (outcome "travelling"). With this field the call waits up to that many milliseconds for the journey to end and then returns the arrival observation; journey says whether you arrived, were stopped elsewhere, or are still travelling (the host may cap the wait). Without it the call returns as soon as the journey starts.
